name: VNC (Virtual Network Computing) to the Internet
description: Detects network traffic from an internal system to an external system on VNC-related ports 5800 through 5810. This shows outbound VNC-related activity; it does not prove that a VNC session was established, remote control occurred, or data was transferred.
note:
Investigation

1. Check the internal source, external destination, exact port, time, firewall action, and whether the traffic was allowed.
2. Confirm the source owner and whether the destination is an approved remote-support service or business system.
3. Check endpoint, authentication, VNC, and process records for the user or application that created the connection.
4. Review related DNS, threat, remote-access, and repeated-connection alerts.

Response

Do not automatically block or isolate the system from this alert alone. Confirm the business purpose with the system owner. Escalate unexplained or unauthorised outbound VNC activity through the approved incident-response process.
author: Elastic
false_positives: VNC connections may be made directly to Linux cloud server instances but such connections are usually made only by engineers. VNC is less common than SSH or RDP but may be required by some work flows such as remote access and support for specialized software products or servers. Such work-flows are usually known and not unexpected. Usage that is unfamiliar to server or network owners can be unexpected and suspicious.
